paper_title: SuperBPE: Space Travel for Language Models

experiments.experiment_name: SuperBPE: Space Travel for Language Models
experiments.research_goal: To improve tokenization efficiency and semantic representation in language models, particularly for handling multi-word expressions and whitespace bridging.

methods.name: SuperBPE
methods.description: A tokenization algorithm that uses a pretokenization curriculum to learn subwords and superwords, improving encoding efficiency and semantic representation.

datasets.name: OLMO2
datasets.description: A pretraining corpus used for training the models, containing a subset of the OLMO2 pretraining mix.

key_results: SuperBPE achieves 33% fewer tokens than BPE for fixed text when using 200k vocabulary size.
SuperBPE improves downstream task performance by 4.0% on average.
SuperBPE outperforms BPE in 25 out of 30 tasks, with the largest gains in multiple-choice tasks.
experiments.conclusion: SuperBPE builds on the natural observation that tokens need not be limited to subwords, extending the BPE algorithm to superword tokens. When replacing subword BPE tokenizers with SuperBPE tokenizers in pretraining, we find that language models achieve better performance over a large suite of downstream tasks, while also being substantially more efficient at inference time. These benefits are achieved without modifying the underlying model architecture, making SuperBPE a compelling alternative to BPE that seamlessly integrates with modern language model ecosyste.

research_problem: Tokenization efficiency and semantic representation in language models
